- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true +10%), apply a “mean reversion” penalty: subtract 2–5% from next 3 periods to prevent overhang.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >5% from true, adjust toward historical 30-day moving average.  
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3 days, align forecast with sentiment reversal lag — delay or dampen reaction by 1–2 periods.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., >10% from 30d MA), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect diminishing momentum.
